picks.excerpt: A games industry lawyer says no-AI clauses have become 'just boilerplate' in 2026 client contracts, because the legal liability and player backlash outweigh any production saving. The contract layer is quietly becoming the place where studios decide which AI tools artists and writers may actually touch.
picks.rationale: The AI-or-not decision has moved from studio policy to the contract you sign — this is the layer that now decides which tools an artist may legally open.

picks.excerpt: Unity published a practical guide to driving GitHub Copilot against a Unity project — context setup, prompt patterns and where the assistant reliably helps versus where it produces plausible-but-wrong engine code. Vendor-level guidance on AI coding assistants is now shipping as first-party documentation rather than community folklore.
picks.rationale: First-party engine guidance you can apply the same afternoon, and a sign that AI-assistant practice is now vendor-documented rather than folklore.

picks.excerpt: The developer of viral Pokemon PC recompilation Gen1Recomp added beta Gold support and used the moment to draw a hard line between AI-assisted engineering and vibe coding: 'was AI used? yes... Specifically, using AI = vibe coding. Which is not true.' It is a rare, concrete articulation of where working developers now place the boundary between assistant and author.
picks.rationale: A working dev states the assistant-versus-author line in plain terms — the disclosure vocabulary every AI-assisted maker is about to need.

picks.excerpt: Amazon Prime Video premiered 'Castle Walls', billed as the first entirely AI-generated long-form drama on a major global streaming platform — two 15-minute episodes drawing on the Alamut Castle legend at the center of Assassin's Creed Mirage. It was generated by AYDNA, a proprietary video diffusion model trained exclusively on producer Ay Yapim's own licensed catalogue, while dubbing, performances and every narrative decision stayed human.
picks.rationale: A rights-cleaned, studio-owned training set plus a hand-drawn pre-AI sketch stage is the first concrete template for how a licensed generative pipeline gets credited — and the two episodes, made two years apart, show the tooling shift inside one series.

picks.excerpt: A wave of fan translation patches — Kamaitachi no Yoru, Innocent Tears, London Spirit Detectives, Kowloon's Gate — shipped with explicit 'no AI was used' notices, as translators describe machine-translated patches poisoning a game's only English version and one professional losing clients to AI before they came back asking him to fix the mess.
picks.rationale: 'No AI was used' has become a shipping label rather than a stance — a live example of provenance disclosure being invented from the bottom up by the people doing the work.
